source_limits: Lu-Phung Theorem4.2 primary proof omits details; not reconstructed here.
Smooth reference Gauduchon theorem does not apply to a rough MA Hessian.
Harnack theorem retains pure-Hessian and extra moment conditions.
Measure-valued mixed-product linearization does not establish absolute continuity or a product with arbitrary Lp(dV) equivalence classes.
No exhaustive nonexistence or novelty assertion.

notes.summary: Bounded primary-source search through 13 October 2026 did not establish the full singleton statement or an actual counterexample. An exact remaining target is an o(t) symmetric concavity gap.
notes.detailedSummary: The inspected stability, mixed-product, linearized-equation and Gauduchon results do not establish uniqueness of the supporting probability for every continuous F. From the task’s assumptions alone, the symmetric concavity gap divided by t converges to the width of A_0(F) evaluated on the direction H. Proving that this limit vanishes for every smooth H would settle the question.
notes.text:
No complete proof or compact Hermitian counterexample with two distinct supporting probabilities was established in this search. This is a bounded search outcome, not a claim that no such theorem exists. Relevant full-text passages were inspected in Kołodziej–Nguyen, Nguyen, Dinew, Lu–Phung–Tô, Lu–Phung, Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, Wang–Zhou, Xu, Pan, Dang, Chen–Zhang and Wikström; the source-specific findings and limitations follow below.

Here is a precise remaining target, reconstructed using only the supplied background. For F,H∈C(X), put b(t)=B_0(F+tH). Then
b′_+(0)=−max_{ν∈A_0(F)}∫H dν,
b′_−(0)=−min_{ν∈A_0(F)}∫H dν.
Consequently,
lim_{t↓0}[2B_0(F)−B_0(F+tH)−B_0(F−tH)]/t
=max_{ν∈A_0(F)}∫H dν−min_{ν∈A_0(F)}∫H dν.

Proof: supporting probabilities at F and G give |B_0(G)−B_0(F)|≤||G−F||∞. Thus b is Lipschitz and its finite one-sided derivatives exist by concavity. For t>0 and any ν∈A_0(F), the supporting inequality gives [b(t)−b(0)]/t≤−∫H dν. Conversely, choose ν_t∈A_0(F+tH). Its inequality evaluated at F gives [b(t)−b(0)]/t≥−∫H dν_t. Along a sequence t↓0, probability compactness gives a weak limit ν*. Passing the defining inequality for ν_t to the limit, using continuity of B_0, proves ν*∈A_0(F). The two bounds establish the right derivative formula. Replacing H by −H establishes the left formula and the displayed gap identity.

Therefore it suffices to prove, for every continuous F and every smooth real H,
2B_0(F)−B_0(F+tH)−B_0(F−tH)=o(t).
Smooth directions suffice because they are uniformly dense in C(X) and separate distinct Borel probabilities. This formulation requires no rough-current product. Equivalently, using the task’s maximizing-current representation, one must prove Γ_F(T_1)=Γ_F(T_2) for every pair of exact maximizers; uniqueness of T itself is unnecessary.

The inspected literature provides estimates and some well-defined mixed products, but no verified argument forcing this gap to vanish. No exceptional continuous F was found whose two proposed probabilities were verified against the supporting inequality for every G. All conclusions preserve smooth positive ω and strictly positive exp(F).

For source conventions, if dd^c_paper=κ dd^c_task, replace the paper’s potential u by κu. This preserves the reference form, densities, regularity hypotheses and estimate exponents, while changing constants.

notes.summary: Kołodziej–Nguyen’s stability and regularity theorems apply to positive continuous densities, but yield potential estimates rather than supporting-probability uniqueness.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem A requires continuous normalized solutions, L^p densities with p>1, and f≥c>0; its stability exponent is any α<1/(n+1). Theorem B gives Hölder potentials. Theorem C assumes a smooth function of both potential and position, so it does not upgrade arbitrary continuous logarithmic densities to smooth Hessians.
notes.text:
Inspected [Kołodziej–Nguyen, arXiv:1501.05749v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.05749v4), printed pp. 2–3, Theorems A–C.

On a compact Hermitian manifold, Theorem A assumes nonnegative f,g∈L^p(ω^n), p>1, positive integrals, continuous ω-psh solutions ω_u^n=fω^n and ω_v^n=gω^n, sup u=sup v=0, and f≥c>0. For 0<α<1/(n+1), it gives ||u−v||∞≤C||f−g||_p^α.

Theorem B assumes f>c>0 and f∈L^p, and gives Hölder exponents α<2/[p* n(n+1)+1], where p*=p/(p−1). Theorem C instead assumes ω_u^n=exp(−Q(u,z))ω^n with Q smooth on ℝ×X and concludes u is smooth; its decisive passage is “where F : R × X → R is smooth.”

These are estimates and regularity statements for potentials. They do not supply the rough adjoint uniqueness required by P16.

notes.summary: Lu–Phung–Tô improve stability to exponent 1/n and prove Hölder regularity, without identifying the normalization scalar’s derivative.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem 1.3 retains f≥c>0 for normalized potential stability. Corollary 3.6 controls normalization constants for nonzero nonnegative L^p densities. Theorem 1.5 gives Hölder potentials for all nonzero nonnegative L^p densities. These conclusions do not provide Hessian regularity or adjoint uniqueness.
notes.text:
Inspected [Lu–Phung–Tô, AIF 71 (2021)](https://aif.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.5802/aif.3436.pdf), Theorem 1.3, p. 2021; Theorem 1.5, p. 2023; Corollary 3.6, p. 2031.

For continuous ω-psh u,v with equal zero suprema, ω_u^n=fω^n, ω_v^n=gω^n, nonnegative f,g∈L^p, p>1, and f≥c>0, Theorem 1.3 gives ||u−v||∞≤C||f−g||_p^(1/n). Constants depend on geometry, p, c, L^p upper bounds and a positive lower bound for ||g||_{1/n}.

Corollary 3.6 gives |c_f−c_g|≤C||f−g||_p^(1/n), with analogous bounds for both nonzero densities. Theorem 1.5 gives every bounded solution Hölder exponent α<2/(nq+1), q=p/(p−1).

The paper describes Corollary 3.6 as “a stability estimate for the MA-constant.” It does not establish differentiability of that constant.

notes.summary: Lu–Phung 2025 gives Lipschitz control relevant to P16; the theorem’s proof is omitted, and bounded difference quotients do not establish their unique limit.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem 4.2 requires probability densities in L^p, p>1, both uniformly positive. It bounds normalized potential differences and log normalization differences by the L^{np} difference of density roots. Applied to F+tH, it gives O(|t|) potential variation, but no derivative or supporting-probability uniqueness.
notes.text:
Inspected [Lu–Phung, Theorem 4.2, printed p. 13](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.18281v1), also [published §4](https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1112/blms.70149).

For probability densities f,g∈L^p, p>1, min(f,g)≥m>0, and sup-normalized solutions ω_u^n=e^{a_f}fω^n, ω_v^n=e^{a_g}gω^n, it states
||u−v||∞+|a_f−a_g|≤C||f^(1/n)−g^(1/n)||_{np}.
C depends on m,p,X,ω and L^p upper bounds. The proof says “we leave the details to the interested reader.”

For the task, set r_F=e^F dV/ω^n, M_F=∫e^F dV and f_F=r_F/M_F. Then B_0(F)=a_{f_F}−log M_F. Since ||log(f_{F+tH}/f_F)||∞≤2|t|||H||∞, the stated estimate gives ||u_{F+tH}−u_F||∞=O(|t|).

This application is elementary; convergence and uniqueness of the difference quotients remain unproved.

notes.summary: The inspected mixed Monge–Ampère theorems establish inequalities for potential-generated products, not the equality rigidity needed for arbitrary maximizing currents.
notes.detailedSummary: Dinew’s theorem requires a reference measure vanishing on pluripolar sets and functions in a domain of definition of the Monge–Ampère operator. Nguyen supplies the bounded-potential Hermitian inequality. Neither inspected statement identifies arbitrary maximizing dd^c-closed currents or proves uniqueness of their determinant-weighted probabilities.
notes.text:
Inspected [Dinew, Theorem 1.3, printed p. 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0705.0974v1). If μ vanishes on pluripolar sets, u_i are psh with well-defined Monge–Ampère operators in the specified Cegrell/local domains of definition, f_i≥0 are μ-integrable, and (dd^c u_i)^n≥f_iμ, then
 dd^c u_1∧⋯∧dd^c u_n≥(f_1⋯f_n)^(1/n)μ.
This is an inequality; the inspected theorem supplies no equality-rigidity statement for P16’s dual currents.

Inspected [Nguyen, Lemma 1.9, printed pp. 12–13](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.00891v1). For bounded ω-psh u,v and nonnegative f,g∈L^1(ω^n) with ω_u^n≥fω^n and ω_v^n≥gω^n, it gives
ω_u^k∧ω_v^(n−k)≥f^(k/n)g^((n−k)/n)ω^n,
including the corresponding determinant-root inequality for convex combinations.

An arbitrary positive dd^c-closed (n−1,n−1) maximizing current is not assumed to have this potential-generated form. Thus these theorems do not justify either its identification with a weighted cofactor current or uniqueness of that weight.

notes.summary: Boucksom–Guedj–Lu defines a restricted measure-valued linearization; extending it to rough adjoint densities remains unsupported.
notes.detailedSummary: Bounded-potential products are defined by multilinear expansion. The general non-pluripolar extension additionally assumes the bounded mass property. Smooth test functions therefore admit a justified measure-valued linearization at bounded u, but this does not define a function-valued operator or products with arbitrary L^p(dV) weights.
notes.text:
Inspected [Boucksom–Guedj–Lu, §2.1 equations (2.2)–(2.3), p. 12; §2.2 Theorem 2.2, p. 14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.01090v1), and the [2025 publisher full text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s42543-025-00105-2). Products of θ_i+dd^cφ_i are constructed for smooth θ_i and bounded quasi-psh φ_i. The general extension in §2.2 assumes X “has the bounded mass property”; this is not needed for bounded potentials.

For task u, S=ω+dd^cu, define C_u(ψ)=n dd^cψ∧S^(n−1), ψ∈C∞(X). The cited expansion and smooth wedge multiplication make this a finite signed measure. Multilinearity gives (S+t dd^cψ)^n=S^n+tC_u(ψ)+O(t²) as currents.

This linearizes the signed polynomial on smooth tests. It neither proves differentiability of solution paths nor establishes C_u(ψ)≪dV. An L^p(dV) equivalence class also need not define a multiplier on the trace measure of S^(n−1). Adjoint-probability uniqueness does not follow.

notes.summary: Wang–Zhou’s weak linearized Harnack theorem retains a smooth background potential and additional cofactor-trace integrability.
notes.detailedSummary: For k=n, Theorem 1.4 assumes smooth strictly psh u, two-sided determinant bounds, a nonnegative W^{1,2} solution, forcing in L^q with q>n, and a cofactor-trace moment with exponent q_0>n. It is a local divergence-form result, without a general rough Hermitian adjoint uniqueness conclusion.
notes.text:
Inspected [Wang–Zhou, Theorem 1.4 and equation (1.7), pp. 3–5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.10530v2).

For k=n, let u be smooth strictly psh on bounded Ω⊂ℂ^n, n≥2, with 0<λ≤det(u_{īj})≤Λ. Put A=cof(u_{īj}), U=tr A and Θ_s(B)=(average_B U^s)^(1/s). For a nonnegative v∈W^{1,2}(B_{R_0}) solving ∂̄_j(A^{īj}∂_i v)=h, h∈L^q, q>n, and q_0>n, the stated Harnack bound involves Θ_{q_0}(B_{R_0})^{δ/4}, δ=max{q_0n/(q_0−n),qn/(q−n)}.

The authors explicitly require “extra conditions on the coefficients.” Determinant bounds alone do not bound these trace moments. Moreover, their divergence-free cofactor identity concerns dd^cu; a general Hermitian background has d(ω+dd^cu)=dω. Neither the extra integrability nor the corresponding rough Hermitian adjoint theory is supplied.

notes.summary: Xu’s linearized Hölder estimate requires C² potentials and a controlled neighborhood of a fixed regular strictly positive potential.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem 1.7 assumes quantitative Hessian and third-derivative bounds for a smooth reference w_0, uniform closeness to w_0, a determinant near one, and C² solutions of the linearized equation. Arbitrary continuous F does not supply this neighborhood or the required C² potential.
notes.text:
Inspected [Xu, Theorem 1.7, printed p. 3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.01793v1).

Let w_0 be smooth on B_1 with C_0^(−1)I≤((w_0)_{īj})≤C_0I and |D³w_0|≤C_0. There is δ_0=δ_0(C_0,n)>0 such that, for φ∈C²(B_1)∩PSH(B_1)∩C(closure B_1), ||φ−w_0||∞≤δ_0, and 1−ε≤MA(φ)≤1+ε, sufficiently small ε depending on n, every C² solution v of det(φ_{īj})φ^{īj}v_{īj}=0 has an interior C^α estimate. Constants depend on C_0,n and ||v||∞.

This does not define the operator at a merely Hölder potential. Smooth approximation alone also does not establish the neighborhood hypothesis: δ_0 depends on derivative and ellipticity bounds of the chosen reference. The inspected manifold corollary additionally assumes a Kähler background.

notes.summary: Pan’s 2025 Gauduchon uniqueness concerns a smooth reference metric on a possibly singular variety, rather than a rough solution Hessian.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem A gives uniqueness up to scaling in the conformal and quasi-isometric class of a smooth Hermitian metric on a compact variety. The metric must locally extend smoothly to ambient embeddings. The resulting Gauduchon factor is smooth on the regular locus and bounded above and below.
notes.text:
Inspected [Pan, Theorem A and A′, printed p. 2; Definition 1.3, p. 6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.02759v1).

For a compact Hermitian variety (X,ω), Theorem A constructs a Gauduchon metric conformal and quasi-isometric to ω, unique up to scaling “in the conformal and quasi-isometric class of ω.” Definition 1.3 requires ω to extend locally to a smooth positive Hermitian metric in ambient ℂ^N. The factor ρ is smooth on X_reg, bounded above and away from zero, and satisfies dd^c(ρω^(n−1))=0 there.

The proof obtains local smooth convergence away from the exceptional divisor of a resolution, where the reference metric is smooth and positive. This is singularity of the underlying variety, not unrestricted coefficient roughness on a smooth manifold. Applying it to ω+dd^cu for arbitrary continuous density would require regularity and quasi-isometry that P16 does not grant.

notes.summary: Chen–Zhang’s October 2026 adjoint uniqueness theorem also assumes a smooth reference metric and bounded smooth positive solutions.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem 1.3 and Proposition 5.1 establish uniqueness for generalized Gauduchon equations on compact complex spaces. Definition 2.1 requires smooth ambient metric extensions; the operator’s coefficients depend smoothly on metric derivatives. This does not cover P16’s rough cofactor operator or merely L^p supporting densities.
notes.text:
Inspected [Chen–Zhang, manuscript dated 12 October 2026](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13005): Theorem 1.3, pp. 3–4; Definition 2.1, p. 6; equation (42), pp. 10–11; Proposition 5.1, p. 18.

For an irreducible reduced compact complex space with a Hermitian metric admitting smooth positive ambient extensions, and 1≤k≤n−1, they construct bounded smooth positive ρ on X_reg, bounded away from zero, satisfying i∂∂̄(ρω^k)∧ω^(n−k−1)=c_kρω^n. The constant is unique and ρ is unique up to scaling among bounded smooth positive solutions.

Their operator is L_{k,ω}h=n i∂∂̄(hω^k)∧ω^(n−k−1)/ω^n. Its coefficients “depend smoothly on the metric and its derivatives.” The adjoint and cutoff argument consequently has a specified smooth-coefficient setting. It supplies no corresponding uniqueness theorem for an arbitrary bounded Monge–Ampère potential or the task’s L^p supporting densities.

notes.summary: Dang’s October 2026 revision gives Hölder potential regularity for non-closed big forms, without the missing Hessian or adjoint regularity.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem 3.1 assumes a big smooth reference form, a solution with minimal-singularity bounds, and an L^p density with p>1. It gives Hölder regularity on the specified Zariski open locus. Specializing to a positive Hermitian reference gives global Hölder regularity, not a continuous uniformly positive Hessian.
notes.text:
Inspected [Dang, arXiv:2603.25520v2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.25520v2), submitted 2 October 2026, manuscript dated 5 October; Theorem 3.1, printed p. 5.

Let θ be a big smooth real (1,1)-form on compact Hermitian X. Fix a θ-psh potential with analytic singularities whose θ-current dominates a Hermitian metric, and let Ω be its locally bounded locus. For nonnegative f∈L^p(dV_X), p>1, c>0, and a solution φ with sup φ=0, V_θ−C_0≤φ≤V_θ, and (θ+dd^cφ)^n=cf dV_X on Ω, the theorem gives Hölder exponents 0<α<(2p−2)/(np+p−1).

The introduction describes the regularity conclusion as “Hölder continuity.” With θ=ω>0, one can take Ω=X and V_θ=0. This covers the task’s densities but gives no Hessian continuity, uniform ellipticity, or induced invariant-probability uniqueness.

notes.summary: Wikström’s 2026 variational adjoint construction has an explicit unresolved rough equality step and concerns a different Dirichlet functional.
notes.detailedSummary: Theorem 6.2 identifies an optimal boundary Jensen measure with linearized harmonic measure under smooth strictly elliptic Dirichlet hypotheses. The rough current-deficit equality is left open near Proposition 5.5 and Remark 5.6. Neither functional is the compact Hermitian B_0.
notes.text:
Inspected [Wikström, Jensen Deficits, pp. 14–15 and 22](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.09492v1), also [Theorem 6.2 in primary HTML](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.09492v1#S6).

Theorem 6.2 assumes a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain Ω⊂ℂ^n with smooth boundary, positive f∈C∞(closure Ω), and strictly psh u∈C∞(closure Ω) satisfying (dd^cu)^n=f dV with prescribed boundary value. With L_uh dV=n dd^ch∧(dd^cu)^(n−1), its harmonic boundary measure is an optimal Jensen measure for the paper’s deficit duality.

Near Proposition 5.5 and Remark 5.6, equality between the relaxed determinant-current deficit and the original deficit under weaker hypotheses remains open; the introduction says “Euler–Lagrange identifications are formal.” Thus this variational source does not furnish a justified rough equality/adjoint argument. Its boundary deficit also differs from P16’s compact Hermitian normalization functional.

full_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=1, omega a smooth positive Hermitian (1,1)-form, and dV a smooth strictly positive probability volume. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial. For real continuous F, c_0(F)>0 is the unique normalization scalar such that a bounded omega-psh solution u satisfies (omega+dd^c u)^n=c_0(F) exp(F) dV. Put B_0(F)=log c_0(F). Equivalently, for n>=2 one may use the fixed-density Gauduchon formula
B_0(F)=n log inf_gamma [integral_X omega wedge gamma^(n-1)]/[integral_X (exp(F)dV/gamma^n)^(1/n) gamma^n],
where gamma ranges over smooth positive Hermitian metrics satisfying dd^c gamma^(n-1)=0. In dimension one B_0(F)=log integral_X omega-log integral_X exp(F)dV.
Let A_0(F) be the Borel probability measures nu such that B_0(G)<=B_0(F)-integral_X(G-F)dnu for every real continuous G.
Question: does A_0(F) consist of a single probability measure for every compact complex X, every Hermitian omega and every real F in C(X)? Equivalently, prove Gateaux differentiability of the concave B_0 at every continuous F, or find an exceptional continuous logarithmic density with two different supporting probabilities. This demands uniqueness of the induced probability, and does not require uniqueness of an auxiliary maximizing current.
Known background: supporting sets are nonempty, convex, weakly compact and absolutely continuous. They are singletons for smooth F, for closed Kahler omega, and on a dense G_delta of C(X). In dimension n>=2 supporting probabilities are normalized determinant-weighted measures of exact maximizing positive dd^c-closed (n-1,n-1) currents T with integral_X omega wedge T=1. In an omega-unitary frame write sigma_T=omega wedge T and beta wedge T=(1/n)tr(B_beta P_T) sigma_T, with P_T>=0, tr P_T=n. The weighted determinant measure is Gamma_F(T)=(exp(F)dV/omega^n)^(1/n)(det P_T)^(1/n) sigma_T and is absolutely continuous. Maximizers attain Gamma_F(T)(X)=exp(-B_0(F)/n); their supporting probabilities are Gamma_F(T)/Gamma_F(T)(X). Their densities have uniform L^p bounds on bounded sets of F for 1<p<n/(n-1), and at the endpoint if lower mass is positive. Compactness or these bounds alone do not imply uniqueness. Near-maximizers may have unbounded higher determinant moments even for fixed smooth data.
full_task.completionCriteria: Resolve the full every-continuous-density singleton question by complete proof, or give a compact Hermitian example with a real continuous F and two demonstrably distinct probabilities satisfying the defining supporting inequality for all continuous G. Preserve the nonsingular reference zero and strictly positive exp(F). Smooth-density differentiability, dense generic uniqueness, weak compactness, uniqueness of scalar or potential, and a result for only Kahler backgrounds do not close the question. Any linearized weak operator or product used must be defined and justified rather than assumed. Verify external mathematical premises at primary sources and independently reconstruct the proof.
